messages.text: Onion allergy. Includes shallots and scallions. Yes all alliums basically except I can sometimes get away with chives in small amounts.

Allium intolerance is real and clinically frustrating because it strips out the foundation of nearly every cuisine. I'll lean on fennel for sweetness, leek tops sometimes triggering people but worth testing, asafoetida for the garlic-onion savory flavor.
Need an onion-free pasta sauce that doesn't taste like sadness.

## Roasted Fennel and Tomato Pasta Sauce

Fennel takes the place onion would normally fill — sweet, aromatic, satisfying.

Quarter 2 large fennel bulbs and toss with olive oil, salt. Roast at 400F for 35 minutes until caramelized and tender.

Meanwhile, gently warm a 28 oz can of San Marzano tomatoes with a tablespoon of olive oil, 1 tsp dried oregano, ½ tsp red pepper flakes, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer 15 minutes.

Fold the roasted fennel into the sauce. Toss with cooked pasta. Finish with a drizzle of good olive oil and grated parmesan. The fennel sweetness in the background is what you'd normally get from sautéed onion — no allium anywhere.
Roasting the fennel separately is the key trick — I'd never have thought of that.
